title: Rehearsing the new Artie Shaw band for $65 a week
summary: Shaw, a studio clarinetist, recruits Leeman, Best and Robinson for a 14-piece band; rehearsals begin on 49th Street and they are paid $65 against $25-30 before.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, I hadn't really heard of him, but I went out --
Who was Artie Shaw?
He was a studio musician who had a band.
He played what?
He played clarinet. A great clarinetist.

And he wanted to see me and John Best and Les Robinson, and he wanted to know if we were interested in joining his orchestra -- he had just broken up a small group that he had with George Wetling and four strings at the Meadowbrook, and he was gonna form a new band.
Had he ever played with any other big bands before this? Artie Shaw?
He was a big studio musician. It was between he and Benny Goodman in the studios.
Oh, I see.

Because Benny Goodman had already come out and started his band, and Artie was on the same trail. So we went and rehearsed, we said yes. We rehearsed in New York on 49th Street, the original studio -- his old studio was upstairs, and we went in --
(Inaudible) studio?
I don't know.
Who was there?
Well, there was Les --
Les who?
Les Robinson.
And what'd he play?
Alto saxophone. And John Best --
John Best was on trumpet, and Artie Shaw was a clarinet player.
And we met one of his -- Artie Shaw's old friends, Tony Pastor, who was the one who played the saxophone, and let's see if there are any other names I can remember ...
How many pieces were with you in the band?

14 pieces. Let's see, three trumpets, two trombones -- oh, George Harris on trombone, from Detroit, and I'm trying to remember the names of consequence that I can place my finger on now -- we rehearsed a bunch of orchestrations, because we all said we'd go with them. They offered me $65 a week, and I never heard of such money. So we all said yes, naturally. We were getting $25 or $30 with Hank Vogini, which was on scale. And who should walk in but a few arrangements -- we had stock orchestrations we were cutting up to fit Shaw's style so we could get started as a band. Fletcher Henderson was enough to make us shake in our boots, as kids, you know. He was friendly with --
